achievements.use: The game has unlockable feats computed from finished-game summaries.
achievements.not: Live in-game goals or scoring; those are rules and stay in the engine.

app-frame.use: Every browser game: hash routes, error boundary, lazy screens, start-up, the stage that scales to the window.
app-frame.not: A game's own screens or look; it only hosts them.

audio-gen.use: Making the game's sounds, music and voice lines offline with free local models (release 1.2 and 1.3 assets).
audio-gen.not: Playing sound in the browser (use sound-player and voice).

board-layout.use: A map board: draw the map once in Inkscape and get click rects and adjacency from the drawing.
board-layout.not: Boards with no board picture, or rules about what a space allows (board-model).

board-model.use: Spaces and adjacency as data, with named placement kinds the board resolves.

board-registry.use: The board UI needs to highlight things (spaces, pieces, markers, stacks) straight from the legal-action list.
board-registry.not: Rules for what is legal; the engine decides that.

boundary-check.use: Checking a game's layering rules (engine does not import UI) and that a catalogue's faces exist.

bug-reporter.use: An in-game bug report with screenshot, markup, offline queue and a filed GitHub issue.

bundle-size.use: A vite build must stay under a first-load size limit.

campaign.use: A campaign of linked scenarios kept as a plain log.
campaign.not: A single game's rules or story text (story).

card-harness.use: Testing card effects on real cards with the scenario builder, prompt delivery, choice probe and inventory with stale check.
card-harness.not: Card rules themselves; those stay in the game.

card-language.use: A new game encodes card effects as data: verb table with handler, resume and text slots, validator, every-verb test; the standard verb pack (cardPack) on card-zones: draw, discard, mill, move, putIntoPlay, setAside, recall, gain, refill, shuffle, search, destroy, attach, detach, reveal, lookAt, scout, flip, exhaust, ready, chooseCards, chooseOption, may, chooseNumber, chooseDestination, choosePlayer, choosePayment, orderEffects, gainResource, pay, convert, adjust, seq, if, forEach, eachPlayer, repeat, count, later, payThen, custom; every card move through timing would; words overridable. Recipe: docs/recipes/card-effect.md.
card-language.not: The game's own rules and words: verbs the pack lacks, card text as printed (override the pack's words), when later effects fire.

card-parts.use: Drawing card faces: the layout as the game's own data (zones, anchors per card type), art with a device cache and decode-ahead, printed text with SVG icons inline, tokens at anchors. Recipe: docs/recipes/card-face-zoom.md.
card-parts.not: A fixed face, the game's look, or the zoomed transcription (K203).

card-patches.use: The card data needs corrections without editing the source data.
card-patches.not: Card behaviour; patches change data only.

card-pile.use: A pile on the table: stack at rest, an animated fan to look through it, picks from it, a grid in the phone sheet.

card-query.use: Cards must be searched or filtered by a small text query.
card-query.not: Game-rule target selection inside the engine.

card-zones.use: Decks, hands, discards and play areas as ordered id lists in engine state, with who sees what and a per-seat view for opponents and the UI. Hand, pile and drag UI parts are planned (K218-K220), not built: ask for them, do not build them in the game. Recipe: docs/recipes/card-table.md.
card-zones.not: Boards and spaces (board-model), card faces, or rules about running out.

card-zoom.use: The zoomed card as a full transcription: decoded printed text with icons, engine notes (errata, rulings), tokens, an icon legend and glossary links, rule ids stripped; unstyled sections with slots. Recipe: docs/recipes/card-face-zoom.md.
card-zoom.not: The card face (card-parts), the zoom's layout or look, or the glossary lookup itself (glossary).

challenges.use: Pre-game challenges: a setup restriction plus triggered penalties in the game's card language.
challenges.not: Core scoring or difficulty settings of the base game.

check-runner.use: Running `npm run check` lanes in parallel with process-tree timeouts and a drift check.

ci-templates.use: Rendering a game's CI workflows, full gate and local CI script from one `ci.config.json`.
ci-templates.not: Rules for what the gate contains (repo-gate, check-runner).

debug-console.use: A developer slash console over the engine-core debug edits.
debug-console.not: Player-facing UI; it is a dev tool.

dice-odds.use: Exact dice probabilities for tests, sanity bands or AI.
dice-odds.not: Rolling dice in play; that is engine-core's seeded random.

dice-tray.use: Dice in play, held dice, rolling through ctx.rng and the roll window content. Recipe: docs/recipes/dice.md.

e2e-helpers.use: Playwright tests of a game that need shared helpers.

effect-library.use: Release 1.1 visual effects: the twelve motion verbs, particles, ambience, canvas layers.
effect-library.not: Deciding which effect plays (the game's motion specs and motion-frame).

engine-core.use: Every game's engine: seeded random, tasks and prompts, copy on write, replay, undo, saves, timing windows and triggers.
engine-core.not: A game's rules or content; the game writes its own `GameRules`.

game-log.use: A readable game log derived from engine events through one table.

game-store.use: Every game with a screen: one store over the game's one `defineGame` object (rules, content, seats, start, view, forced, opponent, words): an answer, the forced answers and the opponent's turn after it are one undo step and one paced step; step undo and redo, autosave, load with the undo steps rebuilt; `sim.ts` makes the same object sim-pool's game module, the opponent driver and replay-cli's engine. Recipe: docs/recipes/game-store.md.
game-store.not: A per-action undo (engine-core undo.ts); hot-seat play with no opponent (prompt-host answerWithForced with seat 'all' in the game's own store).

ghost-card.use: A prompt's source card left play and the screen must show its last-known snapshot.

glossary.use: Linking glossary terms and icon codes in any shown text to a lookup, with a coverage check.
glossary.not: Writing glossary text; the game owns it.

learned-opponent.use: An AI opponent trained by self-play (value net, one-horizon look-ahead) when a scripted opponent is too weak.
learned-opponent.not: A first opponent (start with `opponent`), or anything reading hidden state of the real game.

lint-preset.use: ESLint flat-config blocks for a game's engine folder.

market-row.use: A market of offer slots refilled from decks: buy/cycle options, refill at once or by slide, clear, deal animation.
market-row.not: Payment, discounts, unlocks, where a bought card goes; a hand or a pile.

motion-frame.use: Playing the director's motion specs (JSON beats) on the screen.
motion-frame.not: The effects themselves (effect-library) or game logic.

offline.use: The game must install and run offline: service worker plugin, register rule, update line.

opponent.use: A rule-based AI opponent: advice, profiles and memory as data through a fixed pick pipeline, plus decision records.
opponent.not: Trained play (learned-opponent) or tuning weights (sim-pool tune).

paced-view.use: The table must show an answer's events one step at a time.

perf.use: A speed budget for `applyAction` over whole driver games.

phone-mode.use: The game has a phone layout: layout choice, fit zoom, safe areas, the one bottom sheet, second-tap commit.
phone-mode.not: Desktop-only games; some owners skip phone.

picked-state.use: Marking an option the player has picked, as tokens plus a helper.

pieces-3d.use: Dice, balls and chips built in code with WebGL or CSS (no model files).
pieces-3d.not: Modelled or generated meshes; the owner does no 3D model work.

pieces-3d-verbs.use: Release 1.1: the shake, flip, move and settle verbs for pieces-3d dice and balls, over the effect library.
pieces-3d-verbs.not: Drawing the pieces (pieces-3d); a 1.0 game never pulls it.

plain-text.use: Every line a person reads must be free of rule ids (`TURN-07`, `AR-12`).

plan-checker.use: Checking a game plan and listing a batch's line ranges (`plancheck.py --batch`).
plan-checker.not: Anything but the plan file format.

play-stats.use: Records of finished games, totals, best scores and a play-time clock.

prompt-gallery.use: Showing one state per prompt kind and ending, with a check that no kind lacks one.

prompt-host.use: Showing the open engine-core prompt on screen: a widget per prompt kind (a missing one fails to compile), the common widgets (pick, amount, order, may, pay) unstyled, forced answers sent from the store in one undo step (answerWithForced), board picks with tap to confirm (one or several). Recipe: docs/recipes/prompts.md.
prompt-host.not: The game's look or its own kind-specific widgets; board highlights (the game draws those from the option ids).

drag-drop.use: Dragging a source (hand card, pile) onto a target on the board, both option ids of the open prompt: a drop answers as tap source then tap target through prompt-host useBoardPick, with the ghost, legal-target marks and animation.
drag-drop.not: Free dragging that answers nothing (reordering a hand, moving a panel); the look of the ghost and the targets.

prompt-source.use: Each prompt must name its source card and clause and who decides.

reference-game.use: Kit CI only: a made-up game generated through the scaffold whose own check fails when a component interface drifts.
reference-game.not: Pulling into a game or copying as a starter; use scaffold for a new game.

replay-cli.use: Headless replays, golden games and a determinism check across two checkouts.

repo-gate.use: A repository gate: file sizes, secrets, session URLs, runner names, card ids in rules code, art budgets.

resolution-frame.use: A Resolution setting that lays out for a chosen screen size and scales to the window.

saves.use: Saved games in IndexedDB over engine-core's save file and a saves screen.
saves.not: Old-save migration work (the owner's rule: none until the game is complete).

scaffold.use: Starting a new game: one command makes the empty working repo (Vite, ESLint, Vitest, tsconfig, CI, kit pull, stub GameRules).
scaffold.not: Anything inside a running game; it is a generator run from the kit checkout.

scan-ingest.use: Turning flatbed scans into one cropped upright image per item.
scan-ingest.not: Scanning crew boards or anything shipped in-game.

settings.use: Settings declared as data, a persisted store and a screen drawn from them.
settings.not: Game rules options that change the engine (declare them as settings, read them in setup).

sim-pool.use: Playing many whole games with drivers on worker threads, fuzzing, sanity bands, sweeps, the K200 weight tuner and paired validation.
sim-pool.not: A driver's strategy (the game or opponent supplies it).

small-helpers.use: Icon with hidden word, text-key check, paired legality fixtures, relation index.

sound-player.use: Release 1.2 sound and music from one data table on Web Audio.

state-machines.use: Naming a screen or flow state explicitly as a table instead of scattered flags.

story.use: Story, flavour text, panels and splash as data that never blocks play.

counter.use: A resource number with count-up, bump, +N tag, low warning and a data-res anchor for flights; unstyled.
counter.not: Any look, colour or word; the flight itself (token-flights); the stored value.

table-panels.use: The panels around the table, unstyled: log (event words with slots, by turn, seat filter), banner (turn, seat, phase, fires on change), game over (result, breakdown slot, rematch, review log, home), opponent turn (paced-view steps, what the viewer may see, skip to end).
table-panels.not: Any look, layout or game text; the log data itself (game-log); the opponent's decisions (opponent).

theme-check.use: Checking that the game's look lives in its token file, fonts and layout.
theme-check.not: Choosing the look; the director's wireframes and themes do that.

tooling-scripts.use: Small repo scripts run with `node kit/tooling-scripts/<script>.ts` (art check, shots, text-leak, home screen, docs index). Recipe: docs/recipes/agent-workflow.md.

traceability.use: Test titles must cite the game's rule ids; gate configured in `trace.config.json`.
traceability.not: Showing ids on screen (plain-text forbids it).

transcription-check.use: Printed items (cards, tiles, boards) are transcribed twice independently and the owner verifies them before they enter the real pack.
transcription-check.not: Card rules or card-language checks (card-harness); anything that reads no files.

tutorial.use: A scripted tutorial on a seed with the lock that allows only the scripted answer.

ui-helpers.use: Small screen helpers: hover hold, inspect, rule sheet, toasts, prompt keys. For an engine-core prompt use prompt-host instead of createSelection and onlyForcedAnswer.

token-bag.use: A bag of tokens with its count; the engine's draw shown as a 2D flight from the bag or a 3D shake-and-draw (three.js by dynamic import) that never decides the draw and falls back to 2D.
token-bag.not: Which tokens are drawn (the engine), the token faces and the bag print (the game), a game's token tables.

token-flights.use: Tokens that moved between two views fly from where they were to where they are, with a ledger that draws each token in one place at a time.
token-flights.not: Cards flying, motion specs (motion-frame) or the token look.

voice.use: Release 1.3 voice lines on the sound player's voice bus, never twice the same.

player-board.use: A mat with named zones from a layout: each zone fits its cards (largest size, two rows, a fan below the readable minimum) and is a motion anchor; a pure plan plus a React board with slots the game fills.
player-board.not: Where zones sit (the game's layout), card faces, tucked attachments (K245), piles.

deck-motions.use: Cards fly from a pile to their places (deal, refill turn-over, deck cycle) and a pile riffles; piles found by data-pile; timing pure.
deck-motions.not: Which cards move (the game diffs its views), the card look, a market row slide or a fan (card-pile).

track.use: A row of spaces with a marker that glides (drawn row or spots on a mat image), per-space marks, labels from the game's words; a hop-and-fill bar with a badge pop; a step list with one lit step; unstyled.
track.not: Any rule, look, colour or word; turn banners (table-panels); the number itself (counter).

card-hand.use: Showing a hand of cards (or an opponent's face-down hand) as a fan that fits any width, lifts on pointer or focus, marks legal, picked and barred cards from the prompt, reports taps, is a drag source, and animates draw-in and play glide; or, with layout=grid, the phone hand: whole cards in rows with a header slot.
card-hand.not: The card face, shadows, glow, badges, colours (the game's, on data-part hooks); reordering a hand.

card-attachments.use: Cards tucked under or fanned past a host card with a pure footprint, and the tokens on a card: one per token, ×N past a cap, number boxes.
card-attachments.not: Token shapes, colours or fonts; tokens at fixed face anchors (card-parts) or flying (token-flights).

target-arrow.use: A curved targeting arrow from the card that asks to the pointer: snaps to legal targets, collapses into the chosen one, then a hit; holds token flights until the hit.
target-arrow.not: Prompt kinds, which prompts are targets, the prompt panel (prompt-host) or the arrow's colours.
